posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

Back in 2018, Philipp Dettmer, the founder of kurzgesagt, was being treated for a stage 3 B testicular cancer. This was a very serious situation, but it is not a sad story! In fact, going through chemotherapy was one of the most interesting experiences of his life. He was treated with Cisplatin, which, in a nutshell, put his body through a controlled medical violence. This toxic chemotherapy agent is a hero and a villain of this story, but it absolutely saved his life.

Where did the antimatter go? The Big Bang should have created equal amounts of matter and antimatter, which would have annihilated each other instantly. So why does anything exist at all? Scientists are still hunting for the missing half of reality.

What we know about human history is only a fraction of the full story. Much of the rest is like dark matter, invisible to us. We can’t see it, and we can only see the effects of its presence. But thanks to new techniques for DNA sequencing, dating ancient detritus, mathematical models, and aerial and lidar archaeology, we are now able to get a faint idea of what this world might have looked and felt like.

This is what cherry blossom season looks like in Japan. 🌸⁠
⁠
Every spring, cherry blossoms transform parks, streets, and gardens across Japan into shades of pink and white. Photographer @number_shiiix captured the beauty of the season, when the trees bloom for a short time each year.⁠

Comment HOTEL and we’ll send you the list.

Five travel creator opportunities worth looking at right now:

‎
All-femme powder lodge in Hokkaido, Japan

When it comes to showing off, the Western capercaillie has absolutely no competition. 😂🐦⁠
During courtship, this impressive grouse fans out its tail, puffs up its feathers and displays its striking chest to attract a mate. The bigger the performance, the better the show!⁠
⁠
Nature’s very own display of confidence.⁠
🎥: @lydebug
Simba got himself up on the roof and wasn’t coming down without his dad! Captured on @Ring

Every Halloween, this man and Cricket the golden retriever teamed up for the most iconic costumes.⁠
⁠
They’ve been Carl and Dug from “Up,” Shrek and Donkey, and even Doc and Marty McFly from “Back to the Future.” ⁠
⁠
Which duo is your favorite? 😍😍⁠
⁠
By: @fozzcook

How often do you get to cycle down a 14-lane highway?! Every November, Dubai Ride turns Sheikh Zayed Road into a giant cycling 🚴 track, and people from all over show up to ride the 12km (roughly 7.5 miles) route! It’s the first kickoff to the #DubaiFitnessChallenge!

@sobesi captured this incredible moment from above near Manaus, in Brazil’s Amazon, with a spotted jaguar and a black jaguar side by side.⁠
⁠
Jaguars are the largest cats in the Americas, powerful hunters and strong swimmers that are often found near rivers and wetlands.⁠
⁠
The black jaguar’s dark coat comes from melanism, which is less common in jaguars, and if you look closely, you can still see its spots hidden under the dark fur.

Photographer captured these incredible aerial videos at Lake Maharloo near Shiraz, Iran, where thousands of flamingos gather among waters that can turn shades of pink, red, and orange.⁠
⁠
From above, the birds become tiny dots, lines, and shapes moving across the pink, red, orange, and green water. ⁠
⁠
The colors change with the seasons as evaporation increases the lake’s salt concentration and creates conditions for microorganisms and algae that give the water its striking colors. ⁠
⁠
By: @hose

A mini train, your own controls and a whole lot of fun! 🚂🇯🇵⁠
At The Railway Museum in Saitama, Japan, you can actually drive your own miniature train, explore interactive exhibits and try out some pretty cool railway simulations.⁠
⁠
If you're planning a visit, make sure to book the mini train experience in advance, spots are limited!⁠
Definitely a museum worth adding to your Japan itinerary. ⁠
🎥: @via.kat

@dario.nyc and @frjframes captured Auvers-sur-Oise, the small French village where Vincent van Gogh spent the final weeks of his life.⁠
⁠
He arrived in May 1890 and stayed for just over two months. In that short time, he painted over 70 works, including The Church at Auvers and Wheatfield with Crows. ⁠
⁠
Many of the places he painted still look remarkably similar today.

A little beauty secret straight from nature. 🌹💄⁠
In Peru, one of the most iconic red pigments has a rather unexpected origin: tiny insects called cochineal that live on prickly pear cacti.⁠
⁠
When dried and processed, these insects produce carminic acid, which creates carmine, a rich natural red dye used for centuries in cosmetics, textiles and food coloring.⁠
⁠
So the next time you reach for a bold red lipstick, remember that its color might have a very surprising story behind it. ⁠
🎥: @liya

They have the longest legs relative to their body size among any wild cat—an attribute that allows them to jump straight up about 10 feet (3 meters) into the air! Photographer @sjogrenstudio captured this photo of a short-eared owl over the salt marshes of British Columbia’s Fraser River Delta after spending the evening watching five owls hunt. During that time, he witnessed aerial fights and displays and saw them fly low over the grass, relying on their sharp hearing to locate hidden prey. This photo was a winning entry in the 2026 Bird Photographer of the Year competition.

In 2025, ski mountaineer @jimwmorrison made history as the first person to climb and ski down Mount Everest’s North Face via the so-called Super Direct route. It was an accomplishment he’d initially hoped to achieve with his partner, ski mountaineer and National Geographic Explorer Hilaree Nelson.

African dwarf crocodiles are among the smallest and least understood members of the crocodilian family. Across West and Central Africa, they are facing pressure from commercial hunting, deforestation, agriculture, and mining. Conservation ecologist and Rolex National Geographic Perpetual Planet Explorer Matt Shirley is developing new ways to study their populations and working with local hunters to explore more sustainable approaches to their harvest.
